record.original_question: Let G be a finitely generated group with Schreier growth gap f, meaning that for every faithful action of G on a set X, the function Vol_{G,X}(n) is bounded below by f(n) up to the paper's asymptotic comparison, and call the gap nontrivial when f is superlinear. Are there hyperbolic groups that have a nontrivial Schreier growth gap but do not have an exponential Schreier growth gap?

evidence.quote: Definition 6.1. We say that G has Schreier growth gap f if for every faithful action of G on a set X we have Vol_{G,X}(n) succcurlyeq f(n). The gap is said to be nontrivial if f is superlinear.
Question 6.3. Are there hyperbolic groups which satisfy a nontrivial Schreier growth gap, but not an exponential one?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finitely generated group and fix a finite symmetric generating set S. For an action of G on a set X and a point x ∈ X, let Vol_{G,X}(n) denote the maximum, over x ∈ X, of the cardinality of the orbit {g·x : g ∈ B_S(n)}, where B_S(n) is the ball of radius n in the word metric on G associated to S. For functions f,g: ℕ → ℝ_{≥0}, write f ≼ g if there exist constants C, k > 0 with f(n) ≤ C·g(kn) for all n.

Say that G has Schreier growth gap f if, for every faithful action of G on a set X, one has f(n) ≼ Vol_{G,X}(n). The gap is called nontrivial if f is superlinear (i.e. f(n)/n → ∞), and exponential if f(n) = exp(cn) for some c > 0.

Question: Does there exist a Gromov hyperbolic group G that admits a nontrivial Schreier growth gap but does not admit an exponential Schreier growth gap?
artifact.status_search_result: The notion of Schreier growth gap is recent and the question of whether a hyperbolic group can have a nontrivial but non-exponential Schreier growth gap appears to be open. Searches return related work on exponential growth gaps and amenability in hyperbolic groups, but no resolution of this specific dichotomy question.

status_evidence.title: Growth gap in hyperbolic groups and amenability
status_evidence.snippet: A general version of the amenability conjecture proven for Gromov hyperbolic groups, relating co-amenability of subgroups to coincidence of exponential growth rates.
status_evidence.claim: Related results address exponential growth gaps in hyperbolic groups, but do not address the Schreier growth gap dichotomy for faithful actions on sets.
